name: Tretinoin
summary: The original, best-evidenced topical retinoid — gold standard for comedonal acne, at the cost of the most irritation to manage on the way there.
good: Comedonal acne with a long runway to build tolerance; combined acne + photoaging goals.
bad: Applying at the same time as benzoyl peroxide or another exfoliant on the same night — space them out to limit cumulative irritation and formulation interaction.
clinicalPearls: The "purge" is genuinely part of the mechanism, not a sign of failure — new microcomedones surfacing faster is what faster turnover looks like in month one. Patients who stop during the purge lose the benefit right before it starts.
mechanism: Retinoic acid receptor agonist — normalizes keratinocyte turnover and desquamation, directly reducing microcomedone formation, with additional anti-inflammatory activity.
originalFields: Retinoic acid receptor agonist — normalizes keratinocyte turnover and desquamation, directly reducing microcomedone formation, with additional anti-inflammatory activity.
Comedonal acne, and patients also wanting long-term texture/photoaging benefit.
Slow — 8–12 weeks for visible comedonal change; a "purging" phase in the first 2–4 weeks (temporary worsening as microcomedones surface faster) is common and expected.
High initially — retinoid dermatitis (redness, peeling, dryness) is the main adherence barrier. Requires gradual introduction.
Helps resolve existing PIH over time via faster turnover of pigmented keratinocytes, but early irritation can transiently aggravate pigmentation in darker skin if introduced too fast.
Thins the stratum corneum initially, raising transepidermal water loss and sun sensitivity — moisturizer and daily sunscreen are not optional.
Pairs well with benzoyl peroxide (apply at a different time of day — some formulations degrade with simultaneous BPO contact) and niacinamide, which buffers irritation.
